regulation.notes: CA spray-ground rule is Utah-like: 30-minute turnover, surge basin (min 4,000 gal), UV supplemental disinfection (40 mJ/cm2 with automatic pump shutoff), automatic pH + disinfectant monitoring/control on feeders, no standing water in splash zone, misters on potable supply. Interactive features that send potable water to waste with no recirculation and no standing water are not addressed by the spray-ground text read; confirm with LA County DPH for once-through designs.

Turnover 30 minutes or less and a holding/balance tank are in the 2021 manual and 2026 spec sheet, but UV is listed only 'if applicable' and no automated ORP/pH controller requirement was found, so it is not Utah-like. DPH circular letter 2023-30 sets splash-pad warning signage. Private pools go to local building officials and health districts.

licensing.contractor: No general state contractor license. Conn. Gen. Stat. 20-340d creates a state 'swimming pool builder's license' (DCP) for building swimming pools (including permanent spas), but it takes effect only on DCP regulations (see open questions); residential work also needs Home Improvement Contractor registration (Gen. licensing.electrical: Electrical Work Board / Dept. of Consumer Protection license electrical contractors and journeypersons (e.g. E-1 unlimited contractor); a license is required for electrical work (Gen. Stat. 20-334).
licensing.permits: Municipal (Hartford) building official issues building and electrical permits under the CSBC; public pools, spas and splash/spray pads also need DPH plan approval (RCSA 19-13-B33b) and local health director inspection.

regulation.notes: Iowa reads close to Utah for independent-treatment spray pads: 30-minute turnover (485.5(5)b(8)), a water storage tank of 125% of two minutes of flow (485.5(19)e), and ORP disinfection and pH controllers via 485.5(11) and (12) as 'applicable provisions'. Spray pads must be registered annually and need a construction permit over 500 ft2. Coordinator: iwf_like_utah set false because Iowa requires no secondary (UV) disinfection; the table calls a state Utah-like only when all four Utah elements (about 30-minute turnover, collector tank, secondary disinfection, automated disinfectant/ORP and pH control) are required.

licensing.contractor: No state pool, spa or fountain contractor license. Residential builder and maintenance-and-alteration contractor licenses (Occupational Code, MCL 339.2401 et seq.) cover 1-2 family dwellings and appurtenant facilities; commercial pool/fountain work needs no general contractor license at state level (not stated in the sections read). Plumbing and electrical work require state trade licenses.
licensing.electrical: Skilled Trades Regulation Act (2016 PA 407), MCL 339.5737: no one may engage in electrical contracting without an electrical contractor's license (from the board or appropriate municipality), and wiring must be done by licensed master electrician or journeyman employed under a licensed contractor; contractor license requires a Michigan master electrician (MCL 339.5711).
licensing.permits: Local building department (or state Bureau of Construction Codes where the locality does not enforce) issues building and electrical permits under the Michigan codes. Public pools, spas and special-purpose pools also need an EGLE construction permit before work (MCL 333.12525) and an operating permit (R 325.2115); local health departments inspect.

Decorative fountains and sprays in pools are allowed only in depths of 2 ft or less, fed with filtered water (1-005.20).

licensing.contractor: none statewide for pool, spa or fountain construction. Nebraska only requires contractor registration with the Department of Labor (annual fee $40 from 2026-08-01); the design of public pools must be by a design professional under 196 NAC 1-004.
licensing.electrical: State Electrical Act: the State Electrical Board licenses electrical contractors (journeyman plus at least one year of experience), master electricians and journeymen, and registers apprentices; reciprocal contractor licensing with Iowa, Minnesota, South Dakota and Texas.
licensing.permits: Public pools, spas and spray parks need a DWEE construction permit (plan approval) before work; operating permits and inspections are now local (since 2026-07-18). Building, plumbing and electrical permits come from the local building department (City of Omaha Planning, Permits and Inspections; Omaha runs its own electrical inspection program recognized by the State Electrical Division), and the State Electrical Division permits electrical work elsewhere.

regulation.notes: Las Vegas is under SNHD, whose 2019 rule is MAHC-based and Utah-like for IWFs: 30-minute turnover for interactive water play venues (Table 2-502.9), gravity drains to a collection tank (2-1007.2-5), mandatory secondary disinfection (3-log Cryptosporidium) for new or substantially altered IWFs with no standing water, and automated controllers for disinfectant and pH feeders (ORP is named only for ozone). Outside Clark County the older NAC 444 spray-pool rules apply.

licensing.contractor: none statewide for general contracting, pool, spa or fountain construction; the Construction Industries Board (CIB) licenses only trades (electrical, mechanical/HVACR, plumbing, roofing, etc.). A Pool Contractor Licensing Act (HB 3338, 2026) that would have CIB issue swimming pool contractor licenses was proposed; enactment not confirmed.
licensing.electrical: CIB licenses electrical contractors, journeymen and registered apprentices under the Electrical License Act; HB 3215 (2024) lowered the exam pass mark to 70% from Nov 1, 2024 and doubled CE to 12 hours per 3 years.

Splash pads (spray grounds) have no state permit.

regulation.notes: Recirculating splash pads are Type C 'spray pools' with a 1-hour turnover, two inlets and two main drains, a skimmer and halogen/pH controllers; there is no collector-tank, UV or ORP rule, so the Utah-style design needs a variance or is simply stricter than required. Non-recirculating splash pads on public water are exempt from R.61-51. The permit to construct, plans and the contractor must hold an SC LLR license with the pool subclassification (R.61-51.B.10).

regulation.iwf_cite: https://www.dshs.texas.gov/sites/default/files/CP-PoolSpa/docs/25-tac-chp-265-subchapter-m.pdf — 265.305(c)(2): stand-alone PIWFs "constructed or extensively remodeled on or after May 1, 2010... at least once every hour" turnover; 265.305(d) treatment tank with automatic level controller; 265.306(b) "automatic disinfectant and pH feed equipment"; 265.306(g) "supplemental water treatment system" against Cryptosporidium (UV, ozone, NSF-50 product, or weekly hyperchlorination); 265.301(b)(2) PIWFs supplied entirely by drinking water and not recirculated are exempt from circulation/water-quality sections. File header reads "As in effect on May 20, 2010" (read 2026-11-01)
regulation.fogger_cite: https://www.dshs.texas.gov/sites/default/files/CP-PoolSpa/docs/25-tac-chp-265-subchapter-m.pdf — read 265.301-265.308 in full: no rule on misters/foggers; 265.304(a) only requires the initial supply of a PIWF to be potable (read 2026-11-01). Subchapter L text also has no mister rule.
regulation.plan_review_cite: https://www.dshs.texas.gov/sites/default/files/CP-PoolSpa/docs/25-tac-chp-265-subchapter-l.pdf — 25 TAC 265.183(a): "DSHS may review plans for pools and spas... If DSHS intends to review plans, DSHS will notify the owner or operator in writing"; Subchapter M 265.307(a): "A county, municipality, or the department may require... a permit for operation" (read 2026-11-01). Dallas: Chapter 62 (2021 ISPSC) plus Dallas Health Department for public pool operation (https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/DCH%20documents/pdf/BI_Chapter%2062-Dallas%20Swimming%20Pool%20and%20Spa%20Code.pdf, read 2026-11-01).
regulation.notes: Texas is permissive for splash pads: 60-minute minimum turnover (vs Utah 30), treatment tank with no stated volume, automatic disinfectant and pH feed, and a Cryptosporidium supplemental treatment that may be weekly hyperchlorination instead of UV. Features supplied only by potable water that is not recirculated are exempt; the DSHS says it does not regulate decorative fountains unless the public uses them as a PIWF. Subchapter M text read is a 2010 snapshot hosted on the DSHS site; DSHS's own 2021 ISPSC adoption (Chapter 6, interactive water play) also applies to construction of commercial facilities.

regulation.notes: SPS 390.14 Table 390.14-1 sets turnover for an interactive play attraction at 0.5 h (30 min) and SPS 390.22(2)(c) requires a balance tank of at least 4x combined pump flow (both match Utah). Secondary disinfection (UV/ozone) is only an allowed alternative (SPS 390.17(1)(b)); SPS 390.17(2)(b) requires an automatic sanitizer controller on all pools and water attractions and ATCP 76 sets 650-900 mV where ORP controllers are used, but no mandatory UV or automated pH+ORP pair was found, so iwf_like_utah is false. Plans must be by a WI-registered architect or PE (SPS 390.04).

licensing.contractor: None statewide for pools, spas or fountains: DSPS issues no swimming pool contractor license [secondary]. Public-pool plans must be prepared by a WI-registered architect or PE with the supervising construction contractor responsible for conformance (SPS 390.04); plumbing work needs a licensed WI plumber. The Dwelling Contractor credential covers only 1-2 family dwelling general construction.
licensing.electrical: Wis. Stat. 101.862 and SPS 305 require a state-licensed Electrical Contractor (business credential, no exam) plus licensed master or journeyman electricians (or registered electricians under supervision) for electrical wiring.
licensing.permits: Municipal building department issues the local building permit; electrical permits come from the municipality if it is a registered electrical inspection agency under SPS 316, else from DSPS. Public pools and water attractions additionally need DSPS plan approval before construction plus rough-in and final inspections, then a DATCP (or local agent) operating license; so yes, a separate health-agency license applies.
